messages:
maya: Heads-up: during v3-rerank bringup I see NDCG@10 improve but MRR@10 drops ~3.4% on the prod-like holdout after we switched candidate concatenation to inline JSON separators.
liam: rough numbers? can you paste the eval summary?
maya: Sure — quick run on holdout A (10k queries):
```
model: v3-rerank (quantized int8)
format A (newline sep): ndcg@10 0.312 -> baseline 0.308 (+1.3%), mrr@10 0.221 -> baseline 0.229 (-3.5%)
format B (inline json sep): ndcg@10 0.316 (+2.6%), mrr@10 0.221 (-3.5%)
```
maya: Note: NDCG goes up consistently, MRR is the one that regresses.
anita: hmm curious. did you change any priming/length trimming with the new formatter?
maya: only delimiter: we used to concat candidate texts with "\n---\n" between docs, now we build a JSON array and stringify candidates in one string. no other prompt changes.
rob: could be tie-breaking behavior when top-1 vs top-10 rank ordering changes. MRR is sensitive to top slot. Maybe the JSON quoting adds tokens that alter early attention patterns.
liam: do we have tokenizer token counts for both formats? that would show if the prefix length distribution changed.
maya: yes — median prefix tokens increased from 18 -> 26 for queries+context when using inline JSON (escape chars + quotes).
liam: that could move useful candidate text into different KV-cache offsets for LM? maybe affects the reranker pairwise scoring if we rely on left-to-right attention patterns.
anita: let's reproduce with unquantized float32 to rule out quantization-interaction. if float32 shows same MRR drop then it's formatting-only.
maya: I ran float32 locally (small sample): formatting B still had slight MRR dip (~1.1%) but not as bad as int8.
rob: so quantization amplifies the formatting effect. could be numeric instability on early logits. we should try PTQ vs QAT? also test symmetric vs per-channel scales.
liam: action items: 1) run controlled eval with identical tokenizer input (i.e., pre-tokenize and feed tokens so formatting doesn't change tokenization) 2) run float32 vs int8 vs int4 if available 3) run a top-1 focused diagnostic to inspect score deltas for top candidates
anita: I can take (1). will pre-tokenize both formats with HF tokenizer and diff token arrays. also will run the rerank harness with cached token inputs so model sees exact same token sequences across format variants.
maya: thanks. I'll spawn float32/int8 full holdout runs with the current harness and include per-query top-5 scores.
rob: also add a small test: insert a lightweight delimiter token (e.g., '<DOC>') in the inline JSON around candidate text instead of relying on quotes/commas to see if delimiting tokenization matters.
liam: good idea. if explicit delimiter recovers MRR but keeps NDCG improvement, that would be best.
maya: quick sample query that repros on small set:
```
Q: "how to rotate an ssh key in linux"
Candidates format A:
- "Rotate SSH key steps:\n1. ..."
- "Use ssh-keygen to ..."
Candidates format B (inline):
"[{\"text\": \"Rotate SSH key steps:\\n1. ...\"}, {\"text\": \"Use ssh-keygen to ...\"}]"
```
maya: for those queries top-1 flips from correct candidate to near-correct in int8.
rob: might also be worth checking whether our reranker prompt uses position-sensitive cues (e.g. the first candidate gets small bias). any pre-score priors?
maya: no explicit priors in scoring. it's pure model-conditioned scoring.
liam: let's log: per-query tokenized lengths, top-5 logits for float32 and int8, and whether top-1 changed. store as csv and link in thread when ready.
anita: I'll push a small script to reproduce and attach.
ops-bot: deploy notice — canary traffic for v3-rerank formatted-B paused until triage complete.
maya: thanks @ops-bot :pray: — I'll post repro artifacts here.
liam: if we confirm quant amplifies boundary effects, Optimize team may want to recommend safer formatting (explicit delimiters) for customers moving to quantized models.
rob: agreed. also file a model-onboarding checklist item: when changing candidate formatting, run both nDCG and top-1-sensitive metrics (MRR) across quant settings.
maya: will do. tagging in follow-up when test outputs are up. :mag_right:
